punctuation noun

also punctuation mark, punctuation marks, punctuate, full stop, period (punctuation), point (punctuation)

classical

Cic. Mur. 25: interpūnctiōnēs verbōrum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 248, 367

interpūnctiō, interpūnctiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

punctuation, the marking of divisions between words

The verb is interpungere, to punctuate: cum scrībimus, interpungere cōnsuēvimus, when we write we are used to punctuating (Sen. Ep. 40, Lewis & Short). A punctuation mark is interpūnctum (Cic. de Or. 3.181; Traupman 248). Ancient Latin marked word divisions with points; the modern marks have modern names (see comma, full stop, question mark).

Other words

  • interpungō, interpungere, interpūnxī, interpūnctum — punctuate

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 40 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 367 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • pūnctum, pūnctī n. — full stop, period

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 359, 367 · Declension on Wiktionary
